name: rf_string_key_special_characters
sql: SELECT f.join_key, COUNT(*) AS n, SUM(f.id) AS s FROM {table} f JOIN {bc}(VALUES ('quote''single'),('double"quote'),('percent%underscore_'),('中文字符串'),('plain')) d(k) ON f.join_key = d.k GROUP BY f.join_key ORDER BY f.join_key
pg_sql: SELECT f.join_key, COUNT(*) AS n, SUM(f.id) AS s FROM {table} f JOIN (VALUES ('quote''single'),('double"quote'),('percent%underscore_'),('中文字符串'),('plain')) d(k) ON f.join_key = d.k GROUP BY f.join_key ORDER BY f.join_key
comment: The values are rendered into the statement now, so this is where the escaping is measured rather than asserted: the single quote has to arrive doubled, and %, _ and a double quote have to arrive untouched. The backslash key that used to be in this list moved to rf_backslash_value_veto, because a backslash in a value now refuses the whole filter.

name: rf_backslash_value_veto
sql: SELECT f.join_key, COUNT(*) AS n, SUM(f.id) AS s FROM {table} f JOIN {bc}(VALUES ('back\\slash'),('plain')) d(k) ON f.join_key = d.k GROUP BY f.join_key ORDER BY f.join_key
pg_sql: SELECT f.join_key, COUNT(*) AS n, SUM(f.id) AS s FROM {table} f JOIN (VALUES ('back\slash'),('plain')) d(k) ON f.join_key = d.k GROUP BY f.join_key ORDER BY f.join_key
comment: Doubling the single quote is correct only while the remote reads a backslash as an ordinary character, and standard_conforming_strings (PostgreSQL) and NO_BACKSLASH_ESCAPES (MySQL) are session settings the BE cannot see. So one backslash in one value refuses the whole filter, and the two modes still have to answer identically and identically to PostgreSQL -- the filter is an optimization, and dropping it may cost time but never rows.
